literal: In heart they do not renounce, like those who renounced having deceived, than those who live, hard-hearted people there are none.
translation: There are no people more hard-hearted than those who live deceitfully, pretending to be ascetics while not truly renouncing desires in their hearts.
modern: மனத்தால் பற்றுக்களை விடாமல், விட்டவர்களைப் போல உலகத்தை ஏமாற்றி வாழ்பவர்களை விடக் கொடியவர்கள் யாருமில்லை.
explanation: This couplet condemns the hypocrisy of false ascetics. The phrase neñciṉ tuṟavār describes those who have not genuinely given up worldly attachments in their minds. Yet, they deceive others by living tuṟantārpōl, meaning like true renunciates. The poet declares that there are no people more cruel or hard-hearted (vaṉkaṇār) than such hypocrites, because they exploit the trust and reverence society places in genuine ascetics.
